llm.summary: The skill mostly does what its description says (publish static files) but there are several mismatches and risky details you should understand before installing (missing declared requirements, an external install suggestion, and flags that could expose API keys).

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (static hosting) matches the script behavior, but registry metadata claims no required binaries or env vars while SKILL.md and scripts clearly require curl, file, and jq and optionally use $HERENOW_API_KEY and ~/.herenow/credentials. This inconsistency between declared requirements and the actual instructions is a red flag for sloppy or incomplete packaging and should be resolved before trusting the skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and publish.sh stick to publishing-related actions (building a file manifest, uploading to presigned URLs, finalizing, and saving local state). However: (1) SKILL.md instructs agents to ask for user emails and to call the sign-up endpoint on the user's behalf (this is plausible but sensitive); (2) it directs storing API keys in ~/.herenow/credentials (expected but sensitive); and (3) it documents a --allow-nonherenow-base-url flag which, if used, allows sending the API key to an arbitrary base URL (this can be abused to exfiltrate credentials). The script otherwise limits sending auth to the default base URL unless that flag is passed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry (instruction-only), but the script will abort if jq is missing and directs users to run curl -fsSL https://here.now/install.sh | bash in its error message. Relying on an external install script (here.now/install.sh) that would be downloaded and executed is higher risk and should be reviewed before running. The repo does not include a bundled jq binary, so the user/agent must install jq from a trusted source.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Although the registry lists no required environment variables, the skill uses an optional HERENOW_API_KEY and reads/writes ~/.herenow/credentials and .herenow/state.json. Those are proportionate to publishing, but the combination of: (a) a missing declaration in metadata, (b) the documented ability to pass --api-key on the command line (the SKILL.md warns against this), and (c) the --allow-nonherenow-base-url flag that can cause the script to send the API key elsewhere if explicitly allowed, raises the risk of accidental credential exposure or deliberate misuse.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills or global agent settings. It writes its own local state (.herenow/state.json) and recommends storing credentials in ~/.herenow/credentials — both are expected for this type of tooling. Autonomous invocation is enabled by default (platform default) but not combined with other high-risk indicators here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or running this skill: (1) treat the registry metadata mismatch as a warning — ensure curl, file, and jq are present from trusted system packages (apt/brew/etc.) rather than piping an unknown install script; (2) inspect any external install script (https://here.now/install.sh) before running it; (3) prefer anonymous publishes if you do not trust the skill owner, and never pass API keys on the command line; (4) do NOT use --allow-nonherenow-base-url unless you fully control the alternate base URL — that flag can be used to send your API key to an arbitrary endpoint; (5) keep ~/.herenow/credentials and .herenow/state.json out of version control and consider running the script in a disposable working directory when testing; (6) because the skill owner/homepage are unknown, exercise extra caution — if you need to use permanent publishes, obtain the API key yourself via the normal dashboard and verify the here.now domain and install sources independently.
